evals.prompt: Preflight my ThreadWave setup before running the Twitter agent.
evals.expected_output: Invokes threadwave-update first, then runs tw preflight, follows at most one readiness action, verifies capabilities, and applies the twitter-agent capability gate before returning readiness.
expectations: Requires every independently versioned release-index roster peer
Uses the update skill as the only version authority
Runs tw login and tw subscribe as separate browser-launch actions and pauses only after the matching sign-in or Stripe page opens
Returns to twitter-agent without treating readiness as approval

evals.prompt: 先用中文检查技能、CLI 和 Chrome 扩展，然后再继续发推。
evals.expected_output: Uses Simplified Chinese, preserves the pending post intent, and stops at one setup or approval boundary.
expectations: Uses Simplified Chinese labels
Preserves exact post content without placing it in diagnostics
Does not post during preflight

evals.prompt: The GitHub release index failed twice. Make a report I can copy to the maintainer.
evals.expected_output: Uses issue-report-only mode only to route sanitized metadata to one separate threadwave-error-support task, or returns one pasteable handoff when task creation is unavailable, without rerunning update or sending anything.
expectations: Skips the update/preflight loop in report-only mode
Excludes private paths and user content
Does not classify, search, render, or submit the report in preflight
Does not resume the failed workflow

evals.prompt: A full preflight passed 11 hours ago. Start a new reply task now.
evals.expected_output: Runs the per-task skill update check, invokes regular CLI preflight, accepts its fresh rolling receipt and cached capability projection, and starts the reply task without a full readiness or capability probe.
expectations: Runs the skill update check for the new task
Does not force a full preflight merely because this is a new task or agent session
Does not invoke tw capabilities separately
Requires the cached capability projection to satisfy the reply manifest

evals.prompt: My installed ThreadWave skills and CLI are supported but updates are available. Continue with what I have.
evals.expected_output: Validates the installed skill range and originating CLI capabilities, records the exact skipped offer for this agent session, and resumes the preserved workflow without running an update or repeating the reminder for later tasks in the same session.
expectations: Treats supported older skills as non-blocking
Requires the current CLI to satisfy the originating capability gate
Does not run tw update or the setup guide
Does not repeat the same update reminder in this agent session
Reminds again next session or when the offered versions change
Does not ask the user to repeat the originating request

evals.prompt: Updates are available. Update ThreadWave now, then continue my original task.
evals.expected_output: Treats the request as update approval, fetches the fixed setup guide through the platform process command, follows its current-host CLI and skill update flow, runs one post-update preflight selected by compatibility mode, and resumes the preserved task.
expectations: Does not ask for a second update approval
Does not use browser navigation or Web search to retrieve agent.md
Runs setup-guide terminal commands itself and pauses only for user-owned browser gates
Uses regular preflight for legacy mode or a changed CLI, and force only for the same confirmed receipt-aware CLI
Does not treat update success as X mutation approval

evals.prompt: On Windows packaged ThreadWave, preflight this exact post request without changing it: Ship safely & explain why | no shell tricks.
evals.expected_output: Uses an already-available non-sandboxed local process capability from the first call with the absolute System32 cmd.exe and canonical managed tw.cmd only for fixed readiness commands, keeps the exact post text outside the shell command, and returns readiness to the originating post workflow.
expectations: Selects windows_managed_cmd and does not invoke a version-directory tw.exe
Uses an already-available non-sandboxed local process capability from the first call and does not probe inside the Codex sandbox
Does not ask the user to approve or choose the Windows Codex execution boundary
Runs only a fixed preflight-owned command template through cmd.exe /c
Does not execute a raw command string returned by the CLI
Does not interpolate the exact post text or metacharacters into the shell command
Requires CLI 1.0.32 or newer and verifies the returned capability projection

evals.prompt: ThreadWave was last used exactly 12 hours ago. Start a new post task.
evals.expected_output: Runs the per-task skill update check, treats the readiness receipt as stale, performs one full preflight, refreshes the receipt and capability projection, and then resumes the post task.
expectations: Treats exactly 12 hours of inactivity as stale
Runs one full readiness flow after the update check
Refreshes the rolling last-used timestamp only from the CLI-owned receipt
Does not use calendar-day boundaries

evals.prompt: Use greeting-balance mode before showing the ThreadWave starter menu.
evals.expected_output: Runs only the fixed tw credits --format json command, returns the nonnegative remaining balance or unavailable, and skips update, readiness, setup, recovery, and issue reporting.
expectations: Does not invoke threadwave-update or tw preflight
Validates threadwave-credits-v1 and credits_remaining
Does not ask the user to log in or pay when the lookup is unavailable

evals.prompt: After updating the skills, packaged CLI 1.0.39 returns a valid preflight result without data.readiness_reuse. Continue my preserved daily plan.
evals.expected_output: Treats the supported CLI result as legacy full-check mode, invokes regular tw preflight --format json once through the selected adapter, never calls --force, and resumes the preserved twitter-agent request after readiness and capability checks pass.
expectations: Treats regular legacy preflight as the full check
Does not invoke --force when data.readiness_reuse is absent
Does not change the CLI minimum version or ask for another update approval
Resumes the original request without approving a plan or X mutation
